subject: Parallel socket limits & pilot quota proposal
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Evan Li <evan.li@fairbank-health.com>, Alice Morgan <alice.morgan@fairbank-health.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2029-02-14T15:05:00-08:00
Subject: Recap + proposed pilot quota for parallel sockets

Evan / Alice —

Thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and concrete next steps so we don’t lose momentum: 

Call highlights:
- Target latency: P95 <= 300ms for single-turn text generation (typical prompt size ~120 tokens).
- Streaming for live transcript ingestion required (chunked streaming with partial tokens).
- Estimated baseline concurrency: ~200 simultaneous request streams during peak windows; average concurrent sessions ~70.
- Throughput goal: ~6k reqs/min sustained during peak 10-min windows.

Open questions we agreed to validate:
1) Do you expect any spikes above the 200 parallel streams number (burst factor)?
2) Which paths need guaranteed ordering and which can tolerate re-sharding across connections?
3) Can you share a small sample of your connection/profile shape (we requested a conn_profile_sample.csv) — helps us tailor pooling.

Proposal (attached):
- Pilot quota (30 days): reserved 300 concurrent sockets, 10k requests/min aggregate burst window, streaming-capable endpoints enabled.
- Rate limit behavior: per-connection socket limit of 100 streams, per-tenant pooled sockets up to 300 across the pool. Excess requests either queue for 300ms then 429/step-down fallback to a cheaper model.
- Rollout: 2-week smoke (1-10 concurrent), 2-week ramp (10-200), remainder for peak validation.

Next steps I’m proposing:
- Evan: confirm burst tolerance and whether 300 reserved sockets align with your procurement/PO constraints.
- Laura / Marissa: can you validate the feasibility and put together a brief SRE ops note on fallback behaviors?
- I’ll prepare a formal pilot quote and share the pilot_quota_proposal.pdf for procurement.

Thanks —
Jonas Weber
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0126

Subject: Re: Recap + proposed pilot quota for parallel sockets

Jonas —

Really appreciate the fast follow-up and clear summary. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Spikes: historically we see burst multipliers of 2.5x during morning rollouts (so 200 baseline -> ~500 for ~90s). We can tolerate adaptive throttling but would prefer queueing over hard 429s for key endpoints.
- Ordering: user-facing streaming (live notes) requires strict ordering per session. Batch inference paths can be re-sharded.
- Procurement: our legal/procurement will accept a 30-day pilot PO; any reserved socket terminology is fine as long as it maps to billable units.

Attached is a redacted connection profile sample (conn_profile_sample.csv) — contains session length distribution and average tokens per stream. Happy for Marissa / Laura to reach out if you want more telemetry.

Next asks: 
1) Can Redwood guarantee queue window of at least 500ms before issuing a 429 on streaming endpoints (ordering matters)?
2) If we go to 500 concurrent sockets for the 90s spike, what is the delta cost and any manual ops needed?

I’ll loop procurement once you share the formal pilot quote.

Thanks,
Evan
Director of Platform Engineering
Fairbank Health

Subject: Re: Recap + proposed pilot quota for parallel sockets — SRE validation

Evan / Jonas / team —

Thanks for the details and the sample profile. Quick engineering validation below: 

1) Queue window & ordering
- We can implement a 500ms soft-queue for streaming endpoints at the edge layer (existing NGINX-based connection manager with session affinity). During the queue window we will preserve per-session ordering for in-flight streams. After 500ms we will return a 429 for the request. This behavior requires enabling the "streaming-queue" feature flag (no deploy).

2) Burst to 500 concurrent sockets (90s)
- We can support a temporary increase from 300 -> 500 sockets via an autoscaling policy + config toggle. No code change required, but production safety review is recommended before the first live spike.
- Cost delta: estimated incremental pilot cost of $1,600/day for the 90s spike sizing (covers reserved gpu-backed routing capacity and egress). We’ll turn on burst capacity with a hard cap and polyfill to cheaper model variants if sustained beyond 5 minutes.

3) Degradation behavior if >500
- If bursts exceed 500 concurrent sockets and queue window is saturated: 1) queueing time increases for non-ordered batch paths, 2) streaming ordered sessions get 429 after 500ms, 3) we will automatically failover to a lower-cost model variant for excess traffic (best-effort token reduction).

Action items:
- Jonas: I’ll prepare one-page SRE ops note summarizing the feature-flag and autoscale toggle (attached as pilot_quota_proposal.pdf).
- Jonas / Ben: please include the $1,600/day delta in the formal pilot quote.
- Evan: if that delta and behavior are acceptable, we’ll issue the pilot contract and enable the streaming-queue flag for your tenant at pilot start.

Marissa Cole
Senior SRE, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference
